title: The espresso machine, iii
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Friday. The uncle's regulars come for bait and get offered espresso. They don't know what it is. Gully waters it down in a Styrofoam cup and calls it coffee. The Dog Night is tonight; the strip doesn't mention it.

panels.composition: The shack, dawn. Two REGULARS in rain hoods at the counter for nightcrawlers. GULLY behind the machine. WOOD on the crate. BARNABY back, under the counter, as far from the machine as the shack allows.

balloons.text: Dozen crawlers. And — you want an espresso?

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, two old fishermen in rain hoods at a bait counter, a young man in an apron behind a chrome espresso machine offering something, a dog in the far corner

panels.composition: Gully pulling a shot into a Styrofoam cup and topping it with hot water from the bait-tank kettle. Hiding it with his body.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, close-up of a young man in an apron surreptitiously topping up an espresso shot with hot water from a kettle into a Styrofoam cup
brush-pen black-and-white, an old fisherman in a rain hood tasting coffee from a Styrofoam cup and considering it

panels.composition: The two regulars leaving with crawlers and cups. Gully with a dollar. Wood watching the first dollar the machine ever made go into the register that used to be the uncle's.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, two fishermen leaving a bait shack with bait tubs and coffee cups, a young man in an apron putting a dollar bill into an old register, another watching

notes: The first dollar. 'That's coffee.' Dog Night falls this evening; the strip keeps them separate.
